summary: The vector generator, which carries most of this board's own logic, is built around the original 256x4 state PROM. The sequencer addresses the PROM as {running, opcode, state}, decodes its outputs into LATCH0-3 and STROBE0-3 actions, and runs normalization and binary scaling as shift loops on a separate 12.096 MHz master clock. The glue logic in major_havoc_core is closer to MAME's driver. The IRQ counters, the xmtd/rcvd comm flags and the 2.4 kHz bit all copy the driver's semantics and expressions closely, and the Alpha I/O is decoded by exact full-address compares in the style of an address map. Overall this is a hardware-structured video core inside glue logic that follows the MAME driver.

findings.signal: AVG sequenced by original state PROM
findings.note: A loaded 256x4 PROM is addressed by running & op & prom_state. Its output bit 3 and bits 2:0 select latch/strobe actions, and the output feeds back as the next state, as in a PROM-plus-register sequencer. This is not a C-style instruction decoder.

DVX/DVY shift left until a sign-bit change or 15 shifts, while ones are shifted into a 15-bit timer, with SVEC forcing bit 7. This runs independently on the 12.096 MHz clock enable, the way the board's shift registers and timer counter would behave.

The CPU side runs from a 10 MHz clock with divider taps for 2.5 MHz, 1.25 MHz, 4.88 kHz and 2.44 kHz. The AVG runs on its own 12.096 MHz clock with a /8 phase for the sequencer. MAME uses a single scheduler with timer devices.

findings.signal: Watchdog as counter plus toggling reset flip-flop
findings.note: An 8-bit counter clocked at 10 MHz/4096 toggles an Alpha reset flip-flop on terminal count, so the board would assert and then release reset periodically. MAME uses a generic watchdog device.
The out_0 bits 6/7 invert X and Y. STAT X-flip is a ones-complement (-X-1). A sparkle LFSR is seeded from Alpha address bits. Each is written as the gate-level effect the board would produce.

findings.signal: Alpha cycle stretched on vector-memory access
findings.note: Alpha's clock enable is held off while /VMEM is selected and the shared memory has not answered, and Alpha ownership pauses the AVG PROM sequencer. This is CPU/AVG bus contention, which MAME does not model. It is partly needed for the clock-domain crossing, so it is moderate evidence.

The core has an alpha_irq_enabled flag that clears on assert, a counter reaching 12 (MAME tests &0x0c==0x0c), gamma IRQ driven by counter bit 3 (MAME &0x08), and acks that zero the counter and re-enable it. This matches MAME's variables and control flow one to one, not a 74161 carry/load chain.

findings.signal: Comm flags follow MAME handler semantics
findings.mame_ref: src/mame/atari/mhavoc.cpp: delayed_gamma_w, alpha_r, alpha_w, gamma_r, out_0_w
findings.note: Each port access sets and clears the xmtd/rcvd pairs exactly as the four MAME handlers do, including clearing all four flags when out_0 bit 3 is low. They are written as one behavioral block rather than separate latch/flip-flop instances.

findings.signal: 2.4 kHz bit taken from CPU cycle count
findings.note: The core keeps an alpha_cycle_count counter and reads !alpha_cycle_count[10]. This copies MAME's '(total_cycles() & 0x400) ? 0 : 1' rather than tapping the board's clock divider chain, which the core already has.

findings.signal: Alpha I/O decoded by exact address compares
findings.note: Writes are decoded as alpha_address == 16'h1600/1640/1680/16c0/1700/1740/1780/17c0, entry by entry like MAME's map() lines. A board decoder would use partial decoding and mirror these registers.

findings.signal: Gamma partial decode and quad-POKEY wiring
findings.note: The gamma side decodes on A15:A11 with mirrors, and POKEY register bits are {A5, A2:A0} with chip select from A4:A3. Both match MAME's schematic-derived map, as any correct core must.

Vector-to-raster framebuffer, scaling, and roller emulation from mouse, spinner or stick are FPGA presentation work. The audio stage is an RC filter model with resistor-ratio weights. None of these show provenance either way.
